summary: Phase 6.3: clip-mode drill + RT measurement + per-clip results. The final phase of the Video Opponent Mode decomposition (Phase 6.1 storage → 6.2 tagging → 6.3 drill). Engine, store, and UI changes that wire clip playback through the same rep-scoring pipeline the live drill has used since Phase 1. New shared module `app/src/engine/persistence.ts` (`commitRep`, `mintSessionId`, `buildSessionRecord`, `persistSessionRecord`) is the single source of truth for rep-shape minting AND session-record persistence — both `store/session.ts` (live) and `clipmode/runner.ts` (clip) route through it (closes decision-memo Concern 1 + code-reviewer B3). `RepRecord` gains optional `clipId`; `SessionRecord` gains optional `mode: 'live'|'clip'` (undefined ≡ 'live' for back-compat). New `clipmode/runtime.ts:isClipModeSupported()` feature-detects `requestVideoFrameCallback` (Chrome 83+, Edge, Safari 15.4+) per §B5 measurement-coherence gate. New `clipmode/random.ts:pickNextClip()` implements uniform random with no-immediate-repeat, with 200-draw distribution test (each of 5 clips appears 32–48 times under seed 1) and 100-draw no-consecutive-duplicates test. New `clipmode/runner.ts` Zustand slice runs the drill state machine (idle → precue → showing → feedback → ended); `start()` filters to tagged clips via `selectTaggedClips`, `selectNextClip` bumps a `playSeq` counter on each call so the screen's rewind+play effect re-fires on single-clip pools (closes code-reviewer B1/B2), `recordPress` routes through `engine/persistence.commitRep` with the `clipId`, `stop()` persists with `mode: 'clip'`. New `app/src/ui/ClipDrillScreen.tsx` (lazy chunk: 3.54 KB / 1.51 KB gzip) mounts `<video>`, runs a separate rvfc loop watching `metadata.mediaTime * 1000 >= clip.cueAtMs` then calls `markCueShown(performance.now())`, splits blob-URL effect (keyed on `currentClip?.id`) from the rewind+play effect (keyed on `playSeq`) — same React-effect-churn shape Phase 6.2's B2 caught, but inverted. Keyboard + phone-peer input share the same `dispatchCommit` callback the TrainerScreen uses. `IdleScreen` gains a radio segmented control (`data-testid='mode-segmented'` with `mode-live` + `mode-clip`), two new banners (`clip-mode-unsupported` + `clip-mode-no-clips`), and a mode-dispatched Start that calls either `useSession.start` or `useClipRunner.start`. Clip-mode Start inherits the existing phone-pairing gate. `SummaryScreen` now accepts `mode` + `onClose` props; in clip mode it reads from `useClipRunner` and renders a per-clip breakdown (`data-testid='per-clip-breakdown'`, `data-clip-id=...`) for each unique clipId in the rep set, using `cueBreakdown(filteredReps)` so the Phase-5 analytics layer continues to work unchanged. `App.tsx` clip-runner routing precedes live-session routing so a running clip drill is not pre-empted by `useSession.phase==='idle'`. New `verify-phase6-3.mjs` C1–C4 gate checks (segmented control + live default, no-tagged-clips banner + Start disabled, rvfc present on chromium, seeded tagged clip → Start → ClipDrillScreen + video mounted). All four PASS with 0 console errors. M1–M6 manual checklist enumerates real-device QA per §B5 (±33 ms cue-shown precision against real `<video>` + real .mp4). 33 new vitest tests (271 total, was 238; +7 persistence + 2 runtime + 6 random + 16 runner [12 original + 4 regression/wire tests] + 2 session wire tests). Lint + tsc + vite build all clean. Main bundle 356.23 KB / 109.46 KB gzip (Phase 6.2 baseline 346.98 / 107.30 — delta +9.25 KB raw / +2.16 KB gzip); ClipDrillScreen chunk 3.54 / 1.51 KB gzip; CSS chunk +0.83 KB raw / +0.19 KB gzip. Total clip-mode delta ≈ +5.2 KB gzip; budget was +6 KB. Under budget. Code-reviewer (`code-reviewer` agent) returned REQUEST_CHANGES with 4 blockers + 5 should-fix + 4 nits; all blockers + 3 of 5 should-fixes applied before this approval: (B1) `ClipDrillScreen` blob-URL effect split from a separate rewind+play effect keyed on `playSeq`; single-clip pool rep 2+ now rewinds and replays the video on every `selectNextClip` — regression test 'bumps playSeq on every selectNextClip, including back-to-back single-clip pool' added to runner.test.ts; (B2) collapses into B1 — once the video rewinds, the rvfc loop fires `markCueShown` only after `mediaTime * 1000 >= cueAtMs` on the fresh playback, not immediately on the stale paused frame; (B3) `persistSession` closures in `session.ts` + `runner.ts` collapsed into shared `engine/persistence.buildSessionRecord` + `persistSessionRecord`; both stores now route session persistence through one function — regression test 'routes session persistence through engine/persistence.persistSessionRecord' wires this both ways via `vi.spyOn`; (B4) wire-tests added asserting both `useSession.recordPress` and `useClipRunner.recordPress` call `engine/persistence.commitRep` (would fail if either call site reverted to inline rep-minting); (S1) `newId()` and `newSessionId()` collapsed into shared `engine/persistence.mintSessionId()`; (S4) `selectNextClip` now guards `phase !== 'idle' && phase !== 'feedback' → return`, preventing future foot-guns where a precue/showing call would clobber an in-flight rep — regression test 'selectNextClip is a no-op when called from precue or showing' added; (S5) inline comments now explain why `roundIndex: 0` / `cleared: 0` / `penaltyCounterEnabled: false` are hardcoded in clip mode. Should-fixes S2 (phaseRef stale-read race) is defense-in-depth — slice-level guards catch it, so explicitly documented as not blocking. S3 (prototype mutation across parallel tests) is fine under vitest's worker-per-file model. Nits N1–N4 (glyph choice, flush() comment cleanup, banner waitForSelector race, IdleScreen.test.tsx coverage) — N1/N2/N3 left as-is per reviewer note that they are not blocking; N4 (an IdleScreen.test.tsx for the segmented control) is intentionally NOT added because the three-layer test architecture introduced in Phase 6.2's decision-memo locks the segmented-control UI to verify-phaseN.mjs gates (C1/C2/C3 all PASS) — adding a fourth assertion path would duplicate what verify-phase6-3.mjs already gates. Phase 6.3 closes the Video Opponent Mode acceptance criteria; Phase 7 (Webcam Pose Detection) is post-tournament and explicitly deferred per `docs/SPEC.md` §'Non-Goals for MVP' (`'Perfect pose detection'`). The wrapper's next iteration writes `artifacts/project-complete.json` with `final_phase: '6.3'` and `deferred: ['phase-7']` per `artifacts/decision-memo.md` §'Project-complete signal at 6.3'.
